steps.title: Flame a café brûlot
steps.prompt: Put the stages of a café brûlot in order, from the coffee pot to the cup. One stage does not belong.
steps: Brew strong chicory coffee and keep it hot, short of the boil
With the coffee ready and the burner unlit, put the sugar, cinnamon, cloves and lemon peel in the bowl and add the brandy and orange liqueur from a small measuring jug
Light the burner low and warm the bowl gently
Light the warm spirit with a long match and stir gently to melt the sugar
Hold the clove-studded orange spiral on a fork over the bowl and pour flaming brandy slowly down it from the ladle
Ladle in the hot coffee gradually until the flame dies
Ladle the drink into demitasse cups, leaving the spice and peel behind
steps.distractor: Top up the flaming bowl with brandy straight from the bottle to keep the flame going
steps.why: Everything is ready before anything is lit: the coffee hot and the spirit measured into the bowl before the burner goes on, never poured from the bottle near a flame. The spirit burns with the spice first, the orange spiral gets its flaming pour, and the coffee goes in last to put the flame out.

steps.title: Twice-fry soufflé potatoes
steps.prompt: Put the stages of soufflé potatoes in order, from the whole potato to the table. One stage does not belong.
steps: Peel a mature, floury potato such as a russet and square it off
Cut lengthwise slices about 3 mm (1/8 inch) thick on a mandoline, every slice the same, and trim them to ovals
Fry them a few at a time at about 150°C (302°F) for 4 to 6 minutes, until cooked through and blistered but not coloured
Lift them onto a rack and let them wait for service
To order, drop them into the second fryer at 190 to 200°C (374 to 392°F), where the good ones swell within seconds
Fry them a minute or two more, until crisp and golden
Drain them on a rack, salt them and send them to the table at once
steps.distractor: Cover the puffed potatoes and hold them warm until the table is ready
steps.why: Even, dry slices go into the cooler first fry, which cooks them and sets a skin on each face without colour. Only at service does the hot second fryer flash the moisture inside to steam and puff them; a minute more crisps the skins, and a puffed slice softens if it waits.
